correctness.rationale: The Boolean reachability representation is exact for the given OR update. Every n-step walk can cover the original site and the next site; iterates yield T <= nL. Shortcuts must be separated by n-1 edges, so at time n(L-2) an original length-L zero gap retains an unreachable final site. Semigroup <n,n-1> and Frobenius nonrepresentability at n^2-3n+1 give the exact maximal time (n-1)^2+1 for e_0; the first n-1 singleton iterates and monotonicity establish uniqueness. Bernoulli longest-run union/block bounds plus the deterministic O(n) gap prove probability and expectation asymptotics. Exhaustive state-by-state checks for 3<=n<=14 and Boolean path checks for 3<=n<90 passed in verify.py; those computations are not the infinite proof. All-zero and all-one boundary cases are explicitly handled.

Existing generalized initial-set exponents depend on size and may give quadratic bounds even for support of density 1/2; they do not by themselves imply the stated typical scale. value.rationale: This natural primitive extremal digraph is maximally slow under the conventional worst-case exponent, but almost all random starts converge on n log_2 n rather than n^2. The two-tour configuration comparison reveals the controlling combinatorial statistic (longest inactive gap), and the exact leading constant holds both in probability and mean. The result is a structural infinite-family theorem with direct dynamical significance, not a narrow table recomputation or a rephrasing of the classical exponent.
